problems.stem: An AI coach reports your practice take had 16 filler words, a 190 wpm pace, and a 'rushed' clarity flag. Which response shows you used the feedback well?
options: Submit the take because it was your first try.
Re-record the rushed section at about 140 wpm, replacing filler with brief pauses, and keep the pauses that help comprehension.
Delete all pauses to push the pace even higher.
Ignore the report and re-record nothing.
problems.explanation: You act on the specific flags, slow the rushed part, and keep meaningful pauses rather than blindly chasing one number.

problems.stem: Which note gives BigAL a usable self-recording problem?
options: The AI coach flags my open with 9 filler words, but cutting them all made me sound robotic. How do I reduce fillers without losing natural pacing?
problems.explanation: The note names a concrete tension (filler reduction versus natural pacing) so feedback can be specific.

problems.stem: What is a sound boundary for AI coaching on your own recording?
options: Treat the AI clarity score as the final grade on your delivery.
Use the AI flags to pick one issue to fix per take, then confirm the fix with your own playback or a peer.
Re-record until the AI score is perfect even if the talk no longer makes sense.
Avoid recording yourself because the AI might be wrong.
problems.explanation: The AI provides targeted signals; you verify improvements through playback and human judgment.

problems.stem: Which record of your practice session is most useful for later support?
options: The AI flags per take, which one issue you fixed each time, and whether a peer found the result clearer.
problems.explanation: Logging the flag, the fix, and the human check turns practice into inspectable improvement evidence.
